entries.where: claude/source-genealogy.md, Tychonian lineage table, Bouw row
entries.old_argument: Cited creation.com/geocentric-gobbledegook as the source for Bouw's concession that his model is observationally equivalent to heliocentrism.
entries.new_argument: That page is Danny Faulkner reviewing Marshall Hall's 'The Earth is not Moving'. It does not support the Bouw concession. Use the Bouw Wikipedia entry and Faulkner's companion article 'Geocentrism and Creation', Journal of Creation 15(2) 2001, which states the essential difference is a coordinate change from Sun to Earth.
entries.reason: Citation checked against the source and did not say what we attributed to it.

entries.new_argument: The PDF paginates 79-81. The quoted concession is on p. 80.
entries.reason: Page range did not match the document.

entries.where: corpus: ARG-C02 originator; and claude/source-genealogy.md by implication
entries.old_argument: Attributed the 16 sun-motion scriptural proof-texts (Joshua 10, Habakkuk 3, Ecclesiastes 1:5, Psalm 19, Isaiah 38) to William Carpenter, One Hundred Proofs (1885).
entries.new_argument: Verified against the full Gutenberg text (143,011 chars): Carpenter's book contains exactly ONE scriptural proof, #50, and it concerns immovability and the stretched-out earth, not the sun's motion. The words Joshua, Habakkuk and Ecclesiastes appear ZERO times in the book. Carpenter's own sun-motion proofs (38, 39) argue from observed appearance. The sun-motion proof-text corpus is a later accretion; C02 reattributed to Rob Skiba's modern biblical-cosmology compilations. C01 (immovability texts) correctly stays with Carpenter.
entries.reason: Attribution asserted from the shape of the genre rather than checked against the primary text.

entries.old_argument: All 15 R06 item titles attributed to Sungenis & Bennett, Galileo Was Wrong Vol. I (2006).
entries.new_argument: Full-text search of the archive.org scan of Vol. I returns ZERO occurrences of 'Noether', 'Fermat', 'light cone'/'lightcone'. 'Gauge' occurs only as Ron Hatch's clock-rate scale factor, not gauge symmetry. 'Renormalization' occurs only as a complaint about QFT infinities, never about frames. 'Anthropic' occurs three times with the authors ATTACKING the anthropic principle, so the item title 'Anthropic coordinate justification' states the REVERSE of the source's stance. At least 6 of 15 item titles are unlocatable in the cited source and are marked as such rather than refuted as the authors' claims.
entries.reason: Cluster-level attribution was applied to every item in the cluster without checking each against the source text.
entries.caveats: The scan is one volume of a multi-volume work; OCR quality is variable; these vocabularies do circulate in downstream forum material. The defensible claim is 'not located in the scanned text of Vol. I', NOT 'the authors never wrote this'.
